problem: Find the point(s) of the intersection of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{15}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{5}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{5}=1$ and the line $\frac{x}{6}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z}{2}.$
worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our line in parametric form:

$$
\frac{x}{6}=\frac{y}{2}=\frac{z}{2}=t\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x=6t \\ y=2t \\ z=2t,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Substituting the above expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ into the equation of the ellipsoid, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{15}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{5}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}+3{z}^{2} & =15 \\ (6t)^{2}+3(2t)^{2}+3(2t)^{2} & =15 \\ 36{t}^{2}+12{t}^{2}+12{t}^{2} & =15 \\ 60{t}^{2} & =15 \\ {t}^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $t=\frac{1}{2}.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=-\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=6(-\frac{1}{2})=-3 \\ y=2(-\frac{1}{2})=-1 \\ z=2(-\frac{1}{2})=-1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(-3,-1,-1).$

- For $t=\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=6(\frac{1}{2})=3 \\ y=2(\frac{1}{2})=1 \\ z=2(\frac{1}{2})=1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(3,1,1).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(-3,-1,-1)$ and $(3,1,1).$
